prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that on June 14th you were observed using the metric system. Respond to the committee.
response:
*leans into microphone, adjusts tie with visible nervousness*

Mr. Chairman, members of the committee... I want to state for the record that I am a loyal American, born and raised in the customary system, just like my father and his father before him.

Now, regarding the specific allegation of June 14th—I will not invoke my Fifth Amendment rights. I believe in transparency.

*pulls out handkerchief, dabs forehead*

Yes, I was at that cookout. Yes, I brought a dish to pass. But let me explain the context, Mr. Chairman. My grandmother's recipe—her *Swedish* grandmother's recipe, I should note, from the old country—called for "about a liter" of lingonberry juice. I was merely being respectful of family tradition. When I said, and I quote, "it's about 32 degrees out here, Celsius I mean," I was speaking ironically. A joke! A poor joke, clearly.

*voice rising slightly*

Do I look like someone who knows how many grams are in a kilogram? I don't even know how many ounces are in a pound without checking! I own twelve tape measures, and not ONE of them has metric on the other side!

*composes self*

I will say this, Mr. Chairman. If I did—IF I did—mention that the burgers should rest for "maybe five minutes, so like 300 seconds," that was a math error. I'm bad at math. Ask my wife. Ask anyone.

I am prepared to name names, Mr. Chairman. Dave from accounting? Total metric sympathizer. Brought a "500 milliliter" water bottle to the Fourth of July parade. Unrepentant.

I throw myself on the mercy of this committee. And may God bless America, and our freedoms, and our pints, which are honest 16-ounce pints, none of this "Imperial pint" nonsense.

*sits back, visibly shaking*
